capabilities.finding: POST /api/v3/orders/status is the current FBS pull endpoint.
Marketplace token in Authorization header; no credential operations performed.
Required orders array contains 1..1000 int64 assembly-order IDs.
200 response returns orders rows with id, supplierStatus and wbStatus.
Live status enums and sandbox transitions recorded; sorted is non-terminal.
Maximum 1000 IDs per status request; caller shards larger sets.
Status endpoint has no pagination token; batching is the applicable mechanism.
300 requests/minute per seller account, 200 ms interval, burst 20; every 4XX counts as 10; sandbox is 1 request/second shared.
Documented statuses are 200, 400, 401, 402, 403 and 429; missing rows and transport failures remain unsuccessful.
No partial-success contract is documented; success is evaluated per returned matching ID.
Retry constraints and current batch-to-single amplification risk are documented; exact retry policy belongs to S13.
Researched FBS contract specifies pull polling and no webhook; S04 must independently challenge this absence.
Official sandbox status transitions are enumerated; execution is deferred and no sandbox token was used.
WB limit is per seller account and local processing is tenant/seller scoped.
Starvation, request amplification, restart safety and rate-budget constraints are documented.
Order last_wb_sync_at exists but is not updated by status reconciliation; success semantics are specified for Product/Architecture.
These domains are outside the touched status-read contract; only status-triggered side effects are handed to Product/Architecture.
Narrow research of an existing external call does not add a new operator workflow or domain.
